# Citation

Endelman, J. B. (2011). *Ridge regression and other kernels for genomic selection with R package rrBLUP*. The Plant Genome. DOI: 10.3835/plantgenome2011.08.0024. Source: [https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.3835/plantgenome2011.08.0024](https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.3835/plantgenome2011.08.0024).

# One-Sentence Summary

Describes rrBLUP methods and an R implementation for ridge-regression and kernel-based genomic prediction.

# Scope for simitall

Use as the reference and optional backend for simitall genomic-prediction workflows when an R-native ridge-regression or GBLUP-style model is requested.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Marker-effect and relationship-matrix formulations are closely related genomic-prediction approaches.
- Prediction requires aligned genotype and phenotype samples with transparent missing-data handling.
- Cross-validation must respect intended deployment, especially relatedness and family structure.

# Inputs to Specify

- Numeric marker matrix or relationship matrix
- Phenotype vector
- Covariates and validation folds

# Expected Outputs

- Model estimates
- Predicted values
- Accuracy and error summaries

# Limitations and Guardrails

- Prediction accuracy is design-dependent and should not be generalized beyond the simulated relationship structure.
- Ridge regression is one baseline, not a universal best model.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- How does rrBLUP fit into a genomic-selection cycle?
- Why should family-aware folds be preferred for related breeding lines?
